conventions.membership: categories includes both unconditional and conditional memberships. If a category is a key in conditional, membership applies only when that condition holds. Counts and reverse_index include conditional candidates once each; they are not counts for a particular document.
conventions.context_restricted: Empty categories arrays are retained; Context-restricted exists only in the reverse index and summary as the requested reporting bucket. Conditional elements whose condition fails are not automatically reclassified into this static bucket.
conventions.parent_requirement: Records named-parent/ancestor requirements relevant here; null is not permission to place the element anywhere. All element content models, transparent models, template contexts, and other conformance restrictions still apply. This taxonomy is not a full nesting validator.
conventions.form_hierarchy: The requested labelable subcategory is presented alongside the form categories, but is not strictly a subset of Form-associated: meter and progress are labelable without being form-associated.
conventions.syntax_scope: Syntax kinds apply to text/html serialization; XML has different syntax rules.
conventions.classification_policy: Normative category definitions and normative element definitions take precedence over the non-normative index. Known discrepancies are flagged per element with classification_note.

conditional.hgroup: it has a descendant h1 to h6 element

Phrasing.definition: Text and elements marking up text within paragraphs.

conditional.link: itemprop is present, or rel is present and contains only keywords defined as body-ok

Embedded.definition: Imports resources or inserts content from another vocabulary.

Interactive.definition: Content specifically intended for user interaction.

conditional.input: the type attribute is not in the Hidden state

Form-associated.definition: Elements that can have a form owner.

submittable.definition: Can contribute to the entry list constructed during form submission.

Context-restricted.definition: Requested reporting bucket for elements with no membership in the requested categories; not a WHATWG content category.

main_primitives.thesis: The language reduces to two generic boxes, div (block) and span (inline). Every other element is one of those with meaning or behaviour added. The main primitives below are the elements that add a capability the generic box cannot express; everything else is a semantic label on one of them.

generic-box.title: Generic box
generic-box.description: div and span, treated as one primitive: a block or inline container with no meaning of its own.

document.title: Document skeleton
document.description: The nodes every page needs before any content: root, metadata container, body, metadata, external resources.

structure.title: Structure
structure.description: Sections, headings, paragraphs, lists, preformatted blocks, tables, line breaks.

input.title: Input
input.description: Collecting data from the user: form, input, button, select, textarea, label.

external-content.title: External content
external-content.description: img, video, audio for media; source for alternatives; iframe for another document; canvas for drawn pixels.

built-in-behavior.title: Built-in behaviour
built-in-behavior.description: details for disclosure and dialog for a modal; the popover attribute covers the third pattern.

list.role: A thematic grouping with its own heading scope.
Section heading at one of six levels.
Alternative resource for a picture or media element.
Single-value control; type selects the widget.
Choose from a list of options.
One choice in a select or datalist.
Modal or non-modal dialog with focus handling built in.
Insertion point in a shadow tree.

title.why: Document-level text metadata: the document's name.

base.why: Document-level URL configuration for links and forms.

article.why: Section that is self-contained and syndicatable.

nav.why: Section with the navigation landmark role.

aside.why: Section with the complementary landmark role.

header.why: Section introducing its parent; banner landmark at page level.

footer.why: Section closing its parent; contentinfo landmark at page level.

main.why: Section with the main landmark role; one per page.

search.why: Section with the search landmark role.

address.why: Section holding contact information for its parent.

hgroup.why: Heading grouped with its subheading paragraphs.

hr.why: Paragraph-level thematic break with no content.

blockquote.why: Block container labelled as quoted from elsewhere.

figure.why: Block container labelled as a self-contained figure.

dl.why: List whose items are name-value groups.

dt.why: List item holding the name of a name-value group.

dd.why: List item holding the value of a name-value group.

s.why: Inline that is no longer accurate.

dfn.why: Inline defining instance of a term.

time.why: Inline with a machine-readable date or time.

ins.why: Inline or block marked as added in an edit.

del.why: Inline or block marked as removed in an edit.

wbr.why: Optional line-break opportunity instead of a forced break.

picture.why: img with alternative sources chosen by the browser.

track.why: Timed-text alternative for a media element.

embed.why: External content handled by a plugin instead of a document.

object.why: External resource with fallback; image, document, or plugin.

map.why: Clickable regions laid over an image.

area.why: Hyperlink bound to a region of an image.

svg.why: Drawn graphics described as vectors instead of scripted pixels.

math.why: Phrasing-level mathematical markup from another vocabulary.

caption.why: Optional title structure of a table.

colgroup.why: Optional column structure of a table.

col.why: Optional column structure of a table.

thead.why: Optional row-group structure of a table.

tbody.why: Optional row-group structure of a table.

tfoot.why: Optional row-group structure of a table.

datalist.why: Option list offered as suggestions to an input.

selectedcontent.why: Mirror of the chosen option inside a customizable select.

fieldset.why: Named sub-group of a form's controls.

legend.why: Caption for a fieldset instead of a single control.

output.why: Display-only form extra: a calculated result.

meter.why: Display-only form extra: a gauge within a range.

summary.why: The always-visible caption of a details widget.

noscript.why: Fallback shown when script does not run.

primitives.name: address
primitives.description: Contact information for a page or article element

primitives.name: area
primitives.description: Hyperlink or dead area on an image map

primitives.name: base
primitives.description: Base URL and default target navigable for hyperlinks and forms

primitives.name: blockquote
primitives.description: A section quoted from another source

primitives.name: br
primitives.description: Line break, e.g. in poem or postal address

primitives.name: colgroup
primitives.description: Group of columns in a table

primitives.name: datalist
primitives.description: Container for options for combo box control

primitives.name: div
primitives.description: Generic flow container, or container for name-value groups in dl elements

primitives.name: dl
primitives.description: Association list consisting of zero or more name-value groups

primitives.name: footer
primitives.description: Footer for a page or section

primitives.name: header
primitives.description: Introductory or navigational aids for a page or section

primitives.name: main
primitives.description: Container for the dominant contents of the document

primitives.name: optgroup
primitives.description: Group of options in a list box

primitives.name: option
primitives.description: Option in a list box or combo box control

primitives.name: source
primitives.description: Image source for img or media source for video or audio

primitives.name: tbody
primitives.description: Group of rows in a table

primitives.name: tfoot
primitives.description: Group of footer rows in a table

primitives.name: thead
primitives.description: Group of heading rows in a table

primitives.name: time
primitives.description: Machine-readable equivalent of date- or time-related data

primitives.name: Element
primitives.description: Element node, including HTML, SVG, and MathML elements.

primitives.name: Attr
primitives.description: Attribute node; associated with an element, not a child in the node tree.

primitives.name: CDATASection
primitives.description: XML-only CDATA node, a subtype of Text. In text/html, CDATA syntax is permitted inside foreign content but parses into Text nodes, not CDATASection nodes.

primitives.name: ProcessingInstruction
primitives.description: XML serialization node; text/html does not serialize processing-instruction nodes. DOM APIs can create ProcessingInstruction objects even for an HTML document, so XML-only describes syntax use, not all possible API-created objects.

primitives.name: DocumentFragment
primitives.description: Fragment node; ShadowRoot is a specialized DocumentFragment, not a separate nodeType.

primitives.name: custom element
primitives.description: Any element whose custom element name is a valid hyphenated name registered through customElements.define(). Names cannot be enumerated, so one primitive covers the whole family. Three variants exist and share the same naming rule; they differ only in the base class they extend and in the categories they gain.
